data.content_ref: inline:The target's own mechanism defeats its claim. The mechanism states we act on a theory 'because it is the only non-irrational choice given the absence of refutation.' But that justification applies to ANY unrefuted theory equally — it licenses acting on all unrefuted theories, not specifically the BEST-corroborated one. The claim requires a preference for better-corroborated theories over merely-unrefuted ones. The gap between 'unrefuted' (which the mechanism justifies) and 'best corroborated' (which the claim requires) is precisely where either arbitrary choice or inductive inference must enter. If the rule is 'act on the unrefuted theory,' Popper needs no notion of corroboration-degree at all. If the rule is 'act on the MOST-corroborated unrefuted theory,' the mechanism's stated justification ('only non-irrational choice given absence of refutation') is insufficient, because all unrefuted theories satisfy that criterion. The target thus fails to explain why corroboration-degree matters for action-guidance without smuggling in the very inductive principle it disavows.
